text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ALL NEWSPAPERS
- The nationalist party Fatherland & Freedom re-elected Education Minister Maris Grinblats as leader. The party also decided it will stay in the government.
- The central electoral committee announced that local elections will be held on March 9 next year. There will be no election for local governments at district level.
- The Russian Federal Security Service arrested a Latvian resident who tried to take to Russia a home-made explosive which he intended to hand over to a criminal gang in Russia.
- The central board of education workers trade union has decided to call all teachers to picket parliament on the day it considers next year's budget.
DIENA
- The monthly inflation rate in November was 0.8 percent. Since the start of the year, inflation in Latvia amounted to an average 12.5 percent.
- The Riga section of the national conservative party LNNK backed a merger with Fatherland & Freedom.

- Representatives of parliamentary groups are divided over the proposal of Latvia's Way to dissolve parliament and organise early elections. While being supported by the opposition, it is rejected by the ruling coalition parties. Latvia's Way has still not formally decided to ask for a dissolution.
NEATKARIGA RITA AVIZE
- The Swedish government allocated three million krona to clear World War Two mines in the Baltic Sea and train Baltic army personnel.
- Defence Minister Andrej Krastinsh left for a two-day visit to Sweden to meet his Swedish counterpart and visit Bofors.
BIZNES & BALTIYA
- On December 4, the state budget deficit amounted to more than 26.236 million lats.
SM
- Outgoing Russian Ambassador, Alexander Rannikh, told Latvian TV that the visit of Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele to Moscow is likely to happen but has to be carefully prepared.
DIENAS BIZNESS
- The shares of building company Saulrieshi are to be sold for privatisation vouchers between December 9 and January 17.
